line: (AXL)
vault_lines: You get the money, it come with confusion
meaning:
This is the producer tag of Manalla Yusuf, professionally known as AXL Beats. The UK producer has worked with American artists like Fivio Foreign, Drake, and the late Pop Smoke.

He scored his biggest hit with Drake’s December 2019 track, “War,” following it up days later with JACKBOYS, Pop Smoke & Travis Scott’s “GATTI.”

The song marks the first time AXL has ever produced for Polo G, with Pop Smoke, and Fivio Foreign both being frequent collaborators of AXL. The producer notably had a hand in Fivio’s June 2019 breakout hit, “Big Drip,” as well as Pop’s February 2020 track, “She Got a Thing.”

line: Stakin’ out like a date up in Ruth Chris (Ayy)
vault_lines: Stakin' out like a date up in Ruth Chris (Ayy)
meaning:
Polo G nods to Ruth’s Chris, a chain of steakhouses based out of Louisiana. A stakeout is a period of observation, usually of a particular area, looking for suspicious activities, enemies, and movements. He uses homophones, steak and stake, to compare a date to surveilling others.

He rapped a nearly identical line before on May 2020’s “Chinatown,” where he says:

He was dropping T’s, is you stupid? Left him stanking now
Like a date at Ruth’s Chris, we lurking, we been staking out

line: I’m downtown Chicago, on Michigan Ave with Polo and we on some woo shit (Woo shit)
vault_lines: I'm downtown Chicago, on Michigan Ave with Polo and we on some woo shit (Woo shit)
meaning:
Pop Smoke nods to Michigan Avenue, usually referred to as “The Magnificent Mile.” The historic landmark in Polo’s hometown—Chicago, Illinois—is known for its rich history, tourist attractions, and many high-end retailers.

The late rapper popularized the term “woo,” with its origins coming from the Woo Gang, a gang alliance in the Brooklyn area. Woo is mentioned in many of Pop’s works, like his July 2019 debut mixtape, Meet the Woo, his July 2020 song, “The Woo,” and December 2018’s “MPR,” where he raps:

30 (Boom), 30 the weapon, gun kicking like it’s Tekken
Woo, woo back, walk in the party with two straps (Woah)
Walk in the party like, “Who that?”

line: Dropped a song and I got mad lit All I did was give ’em ad-libs, ayy, ayy, ayy
vault_lines: Dropped a song and I got mad lit
meaning:
Fivio Foreign’s fame is heavily attributed to his ad-libs, which have become a staple of his music. They are prominently featured in big projects such as the April 2021 remix of Russ Millions & Tion Wayne’s “Body,” Drake’s May 2020 track “Demons,” and Lil Tjay’s May 2020 “Zoo York.”

The line is a possible nod to his June 2019 hit song, “Big Drip,” which was also produced by AXL Beats. An article from Complex best described the song:

“Big Drip” is mostly stuttering hi-hats with Fivio’s short bursts of high-energy rapping and even louder ad-libs.

It gained traction over the same summer, blowing up in part due to the ad-libs. One of the most used ad-libs was “lit,” which can be heard throughout its chorus:

Big drip (Big drip)
I fell in love with a lit bitch (Ayy)
Crip shit (Ayy)
She wanna suck on a lit dick (Ayy, ayy, ayy)
Couple bitches I get lit with (Couple bitches I get lit with)

line: Mike Amiri jeans full of blue strips (Ayy, ayy, ayy)
vault_lines: Mike Amiri jeans full of blue strips (Ayy, ayy, ayy)
meaning:
Mike Amiri is an American-Iranian fashion designer who gained prominence within the hip-hop community after launching his namesake luxury fashion brand in 2014. The brand’s jeans prices range from $400 to $1200.

Polo G often wears Amiri clothes to public appearances and on social media. He also mentioned the brand’s jeans on the chorus of the track “21,” which featured on his sophomore album, THE GOAT:

It’s a hundred bands in the safe, now I got expensive taste
Mike Amiri jeans, fill ‘em up with knots

line: And that’s like eleven years where you hold a grudge, it needs to be studied
vault_lines: And that's like eleven years where you hold a grudge, it needs to be studied
meaning:
Polo states how angry he is at the world (mainly towards his opposition) and how his unpleasant feelings need to be studied. He lost his first friend T Gucci in late 2014 which is the reference to the eleven years where he’s held a grudge.

He also then lost his other childhood friends TimTim and Lil Ed who were twin brothers and promising basketball players that both died on October 30th 2016, this can only add to the grudge he holds.

line: Send a nigga soul on vacation, we resort to ignorance
vault_lines: Send a nigga soul on vacation, we resort to ignorance
meaning:
“Send a nigga soul on vacation’' means to kill someone, and ‘'We resort to ignorance’’ here means they do it with reckless violence, without thinking.
The words ‘'vacation’‘ and ’‘resort'’ create an amazing wordplay because ‘resort’ also means a large hotel or a place where people go to relax and enjoy vacation activities.”

line: The FN Ruger on my lap when I don’t got a Glock
vault_lines: The FN Ruger on my lap when I don't got a Glock (Federal)
meaning: Given that an FN and a Ruger are both completely different brands of guns, I believe this is a play on words, so FN in this case is might more accurately mean “effin” which is short hand for “fucking”. So he’s just saying he has his back up gun when he doesn’t have his Glock (another hand gun). Both are reliable semi automatic/ modern striker fire handguns.

line: K’s up, killer season like I’m Killa Cam A lot of Ls that season, I was losin’ all my niggas, damn Three years later, whole world know who the fuck I am
vault_lines: K's up, killer season like I'm Killa Cam
meaning:
Polo is referring to his friend Nacurvie Smith, known to many as Killa. He was killed in November 2014 from gunshot wounds. Polo is throwing up K’s in honor of his friend, but also mentioning rapper Cam'ron’s album Killa Season.

Polo is also referring to the Bryant Twins, Edwin and Edward. Polo is throwing up L’s in honor of them. The twins died in 2016, 3 years later in 2019 is when Polo would start to gain traction as a rapper.

meaning: A presidential Rollie, more commonly known as a Rolex Oyster Perpetual Day-Date, is a Rolex model familiar for being worn by a significant amount of leaders and presidents. This timepiece was first introduced in 1956, along with the President Bracelet that functioned as the watch band.

line: Pussy, no bap (Ayy), I don’t bap a lot (No bap) Can’t say no cap, put that on cap, I’m with Capalot (That’s lil’ bro)
vault_lines: Pussy, no bap (Ayy), I don't bap a lot (No bap)
meaning:
A very smart line that includes word play from the gang culture,

Noting that Herbo is a part of “N.L.M.B.” which is a Brotherhood composed of renegade factions from two gangs the No Limit (BPSN Bloods) and their rivals the Muskegon Boys (GD “Crips”) although according to Herbo N.L.M.B. is a brotherhood that doesn’t affiliate with any gangs,

On the other hand Polo G (also known as “Polo Capalot”) according to this tweet

https://twitter.com/Polo_Capalot/status/1312059337397932038?s=20

affiliates himself with Bloods against the Crips by saying GDK (Gangster Disciples Killer),

So Herbo begins the line following the last lines with “no bap, I don’t bap a lot” (Not lying, I don’t lie a lot) replacing “cap” with the bloods slang “bap”, then turns around and repeats it with Cs “Can’t say "no cap”, put that on cap, I’m with Capalot" to explain that it was not to affiliate with a specific gang but he can’t say the C because (double meaning): 1) He is with Polo, his blood “lil' bro”, to the end. 2) According to Polo, “Capalot” in Chicago means “Like, they’re not the chill person. Basically the opposite of chill" So because Herbo is with a “Capalot” Blood, he doesn’t want to make him think he supports an opposing gang.

line: Twin .40s stick together like Gina and Pam (Yeah, boom)
vault_lines: Twin .40s stick together like Gina and Pam (Yeah, boom)
meaning:
A .40 is an ammunition cartridge and gun developed by firearm manufacturer Smith & Wesson, a brand often referenced throughout Polo’s discography.

Polo likens a tandem of .40s to Gina and Pam, a pair of best friends in the sitcom Martin. This is not the first time Polo has referenced the sitcom in his discography, as his May 2020 track “Martin & Gina” likens his own romance to Gina’s at-times rocky relationship with title character Martin.

line: Yeah, livin’ in the slums, we just wishin’ for a hero
vault_lines: Yeah, livin' in the slums, we just wishin' for a hero
meaning:
“Wishing For a Hero” is the title of Polo’s injustice-driven May 2020 track, primarily tackling systemic racism and police brutality over the beat to 2Pac’s 1998 track “Changes.”

While the aforementioned does not exactly mirror the values of “Go Part 1,” it provides insight from Polo as to why he and other African-Americans remain involved in gang activity:

It’s hard to get a job, so we hustle and flip a pack
It’s all a set-up, no wonder why they call this bitch a trap
Life was messed up, a matter of time ‘til that nigga snap
Post-traumatic stress, so them triggers keep gettin’ tapped

line: Tell me what it is, we ain’t duckin’ smoke, we ain’t scared He reach for this Carti’, it’s gon’ be a whole lotta red
vault_lines: Tell me what it is, we ain't duckin' smoke, we ain't scared
meaning:
Polo G builds a double entendre on Playboi Carti’s sophomore studio album, Whole Lotta Red, which was the highly anticipated follow-up to his debut studio album, Die Lit. The album’s title comes from Carti’s reported affiliation with the Bloods gang and his addiction to red lean.



“Carti” both refers to Cartier jewelry and the rapper’s name, while “whole lotta red” refers to the blood spilled by Polo in a hypothetical fight.

line: Young nigga, feel like I’m Trae (Trae), I score a dub in the A (In the A)
vault_lines: Young nigga, feel like I'm Trae (Trae), I score a dub in the A (In the A)
meaning:
Trae Young is a professional basketball player for the Atlanta Hawks in the NBA. The three-time all-star is known for his clutch three-point abilities, earning him the nickname of “Ice Trae”.

Here, G Herbo likens himself to Trae, claiming that they both score victories and wins in the city of Atlanta.
